classification.difficultyReason: Multiply one equation before elimination, then substitute; the final pair requires exact fractional answers.

content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations using the elimination method.

answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by 2, then subtract it from the second:
$$\begin{align*}2x+2y&=4\\(2x+3y)-(2x+2y)&=7-4\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}x+3&=2\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Check: $-1+3=2$ and $2(-1)+3(3)=7$.

Multiply the first equation by 3, then subtract it from the second:
$$\begin{align*}3x-3y&=6\\(3x+4y)-(3x-3y)&=6-6\\7y&=0\\y&=0\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}x-0&=2\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Check: $2-0=2$ and $3(2)+4(0)=6$.

Multiply the first equation by 2, then add it to the second:
$$\begin{align*}4x+2y&=6\\(4x+2y)+(5x-2y)&=6-15\\9x&=-9\\x&=-1\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}2(-1)+y&=3\\-2+y&=3\\y&=5\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(-1)+5=3$ and $5(-1)-2(5)=-15$.

Eliminate $x$, then substitute to find its value.
answer.worked:
Multiply the first equation by 2, then subtract it from the second:
$$\begin{align*}2x-10y&=18\\(2x+3y)-(2x-10y)&=10-18\\13y&=-8\\y&=-\frac{8}{13}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation:
$$\begin{align*}x-5\left(-\frac{8}{13}\right)&=9\\x+\frac{40}{13}&=\frac{117}{13}\\x&=\frac{77}{13}\end{align*}$$
Check:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{77}{13}-5\left(-\frac{8}{13}\right)&=9\\2\left(\frac{77}{13}\right)+3\left(-\frac{8}{13}\right)&=10\end{align*}$$
